what_its_for: Alendronate is used to treat or prevent osteoporosis (weak, brittle bones) in women after menopause and in men. It helps make your bones stronger and lowers your chance of breaking a bone. It is also used to treat Paget's disease of bone and bone loss caused by steroid medicines like prednisone.
how_to_take: Take alendronate first thing in the morning, at least 30 minutes BEFORE eating, drinking anything other than plain water, or taking any other medicines or vitamins. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass (6 to 8 ounces) of plain water only — do NOT use mineral water, coffee, tea, juice, or milk. After taking it, stay sitting upright or standing for at least 30 minutes — do NOT lie down. This helps the medicine reach your stomach safely and protects your esophagus (food pipe) from irritation. If you take the effervescent tablet (Binosto), dissolve it in 4 ounces of plain water and drink it all.
dosing: The usual dose depends on what you are being treated for. For osteoporosis treatment: 10 mg once daily OR 70 mg once weekly. For osteoporosis prevention: 5 mg once daily OR 35 mg once weekly. For Paget's disease: 40 mg once daily for 6 months. For steroid-induced osteoporosis: 5 mg once daily (10 mg daily for postmenopausal women not on estrogen). Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Take your weekly dose on the same day each week.
missed_dose: If you take alendronate DAILY and miss a dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose the following morning as usual. Do NOT take two doses on the same day. If you take alendronate WEEKLY and miss a dose, take it the morning after you remember. Then go back to taking it on your regular weekly day. Do NOT take two doses in the same week.
storage: Store alendronate tablets at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not store it in the bathroom.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT lie down for at least 30 minutes after taking this medicine. Do NOT eat, drink anything other than plain water, or take other medicines or vitamins within 30 minutes of taking alendronate. Avoid taking antacids, calcium supplements, or vitamins with minerals within 30 minutes, as they can prevent alendronate from working properly. Avoid smoking and drinking too much alcohol, as these can weaken your bones. Talk to your doctor before having any dental procedures, as alendronate has rarely been linked to jaw bone problems — good dental hygiene is very important.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you have: chest pain, heartburn, or pain when swallowing; new or worsening difficulty swallowing; severe stomach or jaw pain; pain, numbness, or a heavy feeling in your thigh, hip, or groin (which could be a sign of a rare thigh bone fracture); swelling or sores in your mouth; rash, hives, or difficulty breathing (signs of an allergic reaction); muscle cramps, spasms, or numbness (signs of low calcium); or any unusual bone, joint, or muscle pain. Also tell your doctor if you develop tooth or jaw pain, especially after a dental procedure.
when_it_works: Alendronate starts working in your body right away, but you may not feel any different, because bone strengthening happens slowly and silently. It may take 3 to 6 months or longer before a bone density scan shows improvement. It is important to keep taking this medicine even if you feel fine. Your doctor will likely check your bone density after 1 to 2 years of treatment to see how well it is working.
special_populations: Older adults (65+): Alendronate can be used safely in older adults, but make sure to follow the instructions carefully about staying upright after taking it to reduce the risk of esophagus irritation. Kidney disease: Alendronate is NOT recommended if your kidneys are working poorly (creatinine clearance less than 35 mL/min). Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine is generally NOT used during pregnancy. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Children: Alendronate is not approved for use in children except in special cases. Vitamin D and calcium: Most people taking alendronate also need to take calcium and vitamin D supplements — ask your doctor or pharmacist what dose is right for you.
